fusion: #4 ResAdd+RMSNorm+Router and #5 RMSNorm+Router (+ FUSE_TOPK: sigmoid + noaux_tc top-8 folded in)

fairness.flags: DO_ADD / DO_NORM / DO_GEMM / DO_TOPK constexpr select all seven kernels (4 fused variants + 3 stand-alone pieces)
fairness.grids: gemm_grid() (97 cfgs) for the stand-alone router GEMM; fused_grid() = gemm_grid() x {NORM_BK tied, NORM_BK ladder} (226) for the fused #4/#5 kernels -- NORM_BK is the fused-side counterpart of the k-tile the unfused norm kernel tunes independently over norm_grid() (53 cfgs), so the unfused side sees 97+53=150 configs against the fused side's 226; the FUSE_TOPK variants get fused_grid() restricted to BLOCK_E=256 (100), which is a structural requirement (all 256 logits of a row must live in one program), not a tuning choice; every config of every variant is numerically screened against the fp32 reference before it is allowed into a timing grid (see 'screen' in the bench).  Counts are live for THIS device -- the SMEM ceiling and warp width both prune the grid, and they prune the BLOCK_E=256 family (the fused FUSE_TOPK arm's only legal shape) harder than they prune the rest
fairness.baseline_extra: each unfused chain additionally gets a joint re-tune over the top-3 x top-3 (x top-2) configs of its pieces, timed as the real chain -- this can only help the baseline
fairness.weight_layout: the router weight is transposed to [H, E] ONCE and both sides consume that same layout (a load-time weight-prep choice)
